title: Attribute role typing: identity vs obligation + adapter-declared trivial implications
description:
Per the sutra/176 decision (arc sutra/~12): type the attribute vocabulary so deviation checking is structurally constrained to actionable direction, instead of post-hoc rule denylists.

Classify every attribute at extraction (`src/conventions/attributes.rs`, per-language `as_fca_source` extractors):
- **identity** — what a symbol *is*: `kind:*`, `in:*` / component membership, language, method-ness/receiver. Never a consequent.
- **obligation** — what a symbol *should have/do*: `has_doc`, `naming:*`, `returns_result`/`returns_option`, `effect:*`, async-ness. The only valid consequents.

Only identity(+obligation) → obligation implications are checkable. This structurally kills the tautologies (component-membership restatements) and backwards correlations (`has_doc → vis:pub`) that made up most of the 176 noise taxonomy.

Additionally: let language adapters declare **toolchain-enforced pairs** to exclude from checking (Rust: `kind:function → naming:snake_case`, `kind:const → naming:SCREAMING`, etc. — rustc/clippy already enforce these). Hang this off the `as_fca_source` trait so each adapter owns its own trivia list.

`vis:*` is ambiguous (identity-ish as antecedent, occasionally obligation-ish) — default it to identity/antecedent-only and note the call in the code.

Acceptance: attribute role encoded in the type (enum or tagged newtype, not string prefix convention alone); unit tests covering role assignment per extractor; a test that a tautological and a backwards implication are excluded from checkable set while `vis:pub → has_doc` survives.

2.
